canonical_name: Brooks's 1941 graph-coloring theorem (original n > 2 componentwise form, source admission open)
literal_source_claim_en: An upper bound for the chromatic number.
source_attribution: Rowland Brooks, 1941 (uncited catalog metadata; the located paper is signed R. L. Brooks)
candidate_statement_family_not_credited: For every natural n greater than 2, a possibly infinite loopless network with at most n incident lines at each node and with no connected component a complete graph on n + 1 nodes can be properly colored with n colors.
statement_blocker: The publisher first-page facsimile identifies a precise candidate root, but the complete four-page source has not been admitted or independently reviewed and the source's network/line semantics have not been proved equivalent to Lean's loopless no-parallel-edge SimpleGraph model. The statement phase must resolve those points and freeze, fingerprint, transport, and mutation-test the exact expression without substituting the familiar finite connected modern form.
domain_and_universes: Candidate: universe u; V : Type u; G : SimpleGraph V; G.LocallyFinite; n : Nat; connected components of G; target Prop in universe 0. No Finite V, Fintype V, or planarity premise.
conclusion: Open pending statement freeze. The candidate conclusion is G.Colorable n after 2 < n, pointwise degree at most n, and componentwise non-n-simplex hypotheses.

candidate_scope_not_credited.lean_envelope: forall arbitrary locally finite SimpleGraph G and Nat n, 2 < n implies pointwise degree <= n implies no component isomorphic to completeGraph (Fin (n + 1)) implies G.Colorable n
candidate_scope_not_credited.modern_form: for a finite connected simple graph, chromatic number is at most maximum degree unless the graph is complete or an odd cycle
candidate_scope_not_credited.relationship: closely related but not credited as equality, iff, implication, or source identity until checked in the statement phase
